prs.title: feat(protocol): cap forwarded message_failed rows per reason in the telemetry pipe
prs.body:
## Summary

This is the telemetry-side backstop for the loop fixed in #444. That fix stops
the loop at its source. This PR bounds what the next bug of the same kind can
cost.

**Problem.** The pipe forwarded every `protocol.message.failed` as its own row,
and no protocol event had any limit. A row cannot carry a message id: no
identifier has a field to land in, `docs/privacy.md` and the threat model say
so, and the golden fixture pins it. So the ingest cannot tell one failure
reported many times from many failures, and it meters every row. While the
outbox loop was running, a handful of devices each uploaded about 15 accepted
events per second for days.

**The cap.** Each `reason` gets a token bucket, in
`telemetry/pipe/failure_limit.rs`. It allows 500 rows at once, enough for a full
outbox expiring or being evicted in one sweep, then one row every 10 seconds.
The loop that sent 1.3M rows a day would now send about 8,600.

**No count is lost.**
- Every failure is still counted into the rollup's `sends_failed_sum`, so the
  minute totals stay exact. Only the per-row `reason` and `retry_count` are
  thinned.
- A held-back row is added to `telemetryStats().dropped`, which keeps the
  existing identity true: sent plus dropped equals every event the pipe was
  handed. The three-day soak test asserts that identity, and it now exercises
  the cap as well.

**Where the check runs.** It runs on the borrowed `&Event` on both routes into
the pipeline (`handle_protocol_event` and `handle` for a
`TelemetryRecord::Protocol`), before classification copies the reason. A
held-back row therefore costs no allocation, in line with the pipe's
"never allocate for an event it drops" rule.

**Design choices.**
- Reasons are the engine's own fixed literals, so the table is a short Vec
  scanned linearly. A table that somehow fills puts every further reason in one
  shared bucket rather than growing.
- The buckets live as long as the pipe, not the session, so a device that
  foregrounds often does not get a fresh burst each time.

## Related issues

Refs #444.

## Type of change

- [x] `feat` — new feature
- [x] `docs` — documentation only
- [x] `test` — adding or correcting tests

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes
- [x] `cargo test -p offline-protocol --lib` passes (1,781 tests, 9 of them new). I did not run the full workspace locally.
- [x] `cargo-deny` is satisfied (no dependency changes)
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits
- [x] Docs / `CHANGELOG.md` updated where relevant
- [x] No new `unsafe` in core crates
- [x] The UniFFI UDL did not change

## Breaking changes

None. No wire change, no golden-fixture change, no new reason classifier (the
ADR 0013 rule is not engaged), no UDL change and no new setting. The only
visible difference is that `dropped` can now include held-back failure rows,
and the stats table in `docs/telemetry.md` says so.

## Notes for reviewers

**Tests.**
- `failure_limit.rs` has seven unit tests covering:
  - the burst
  - the sustained rate, one row per refill over a simulated day at 20 per second
  - separate buckets per reason
  - refilling up to the burst and no further
  - a full bucket banking no progress while it waits
  - a clock that goes backwards
  - the shared overflow bucket
- `a_repeating_failure_is_counted_in_full_and_sent_up_to_its_ceiling` (pipeline)
  covers both routes sharing one ceiling and `sends_failed_sum` staying exact.
- `a_looping_failure_uploads_its_burst_and_counts_the_rest_as_dropped` runs the
  scenario end to end through an inline pipe and a capturing client.

**Mutation checks.** Removing the rollup count from the hold-back path fails the
pipeline test. Removing the `dropped` count fails the scenario test and the
soak test's identity.

**Soak test.** `three_days_offline_...` emits the same reason 40 times per tick,
so the cap now engages. Its "the caps trimmed the queue" assertion used to read
`stats.dropped`, which would now pass on held-back rows alone. It reads the
store's own `dropped_events()` instead, so it still proves what its message says.

**CI.** The Test job is red on every branch right now, main included, because of
an expired fixture in `offline-protocol-leaf/tests/phone_interop.rs`. That is
unrelated to this change and is fixed separately.

prs.title: fix(protocol): retire an evicted message from the retry queue and ACK tracker
prs.body:
## Summary

A handful of long-lived sessions are uploading about 15 `protocol.message.failed`
rows per second each, all with reason `"Outbox capacity exceeded"` and
`retry_count` 0. That is about 3.7M rows in the last 30 days, and every one is
metered. The rows are real SDK output, not an ingest bug. The SDK is reporting
the same kind of failure over and over, and the app receives each one as a
terminal `MessageFailed`.

**The loop.** A full outbox evicts its least recently sent entry and reports it
failed. Eviction removed only the outbox entry and its persisted copy, so the
message stayed in the retry queue. `process_retry_queue` and the reconnect flush
both call `ensure_outbox_entry` before resending, and that call re-creates a
missing entry with fresh timestamps. With the outbox still full, re-creating it
evicted a different message. That message was reported failed, and it was still
queued for retry too.

**Why it never ended.** The outbox is the only thing that expires a message, and
each resurrection reset its clocks. The retry queue's own `cleanup_expired` never
fired either, because every re-enqueue stamps `added_at` again. So a device
holding more than 500 undeliverable messages reported one "terminal" failure per
retry, forever, for ids it had already reported.

The numbers fit. At the 300s backoff ceiling, 15 failures per second is a
backlog of roughly 5,000 messages. `retry_count` is 0 because none of those sends
ever succeeded. The new test reproduces the loop: ten `process()` ticks against a
full, all-failing outbox reported 200 failures for one eviction.

**A second hole of the same kind.** A message evicted while awaiting its ACK
stayed in the ACK tracker.
- If the ACK timed out, the message was reported failed a second time, as
  `"Message missing from outbox (cannot retry)"`.
- If the ACK arrived first, the message was reported delivered after it had been
  reported failed.

**The fix.** Every path that gives a message up now goes through one function,
`retire_undeliverable_message`. It takes the id out of the retry queue, the ACK
tracker and the outbox together, fails any media transfer the id belongs to, and
records the transport failure.

| Path | Retry entry before this PR | ACK entry before this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Capacity eviction (both outboxes) | **leaked** | **leaked** |
| ACK timeout with no outbox entry | **leaked** | removed |
| Lifetime expiry | removed | removed (none can be pending there) |
| Retry exhaustion | removed | removed |

Each path still emits its own event, because what a drop owes the app differs by
path. Expiry now also clears staged re-seal provenance, which it skipped before
because it removed the outbox entry directly.

## Related issues

No issue filed. The report came from the telemetry backend.

## Type of change

- [x] `fix` — bug fix
- [x] `docs` — documentation only
- [x] `test` — adding or correcting tests

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --lib` passes (1,776 engine unit tests, 4 of them new). I did not run the doctest pass locally; no doc examples changed.
- [x] `cargo-deny` is satisfied (no dependency changes)
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits
- [x] Docs / `CHANGELOG.md` updated where relevant
- [x] No new `unsafe` in core crates
- [x] The UniFFI UDL did not change

## Breaking changes

None. No change to the UDL, the wire format, the FFI error enum or storage, and
no binding code changes. No bridge matches on the `reason` string, and none
buffers or dedupes `message_failed`.

Apps can see two behaviour changes:
- An evicted message is no longer re-sent, so it can no longer be delivered
  after the app was told it failed.
- An app that counts `message_failed` events will see that count drop to one
  per failed message.

## Notes for reviewers

**Tests.** The existing eviction test could not see this bug. It never drove
`process()`, its backoff was 60s, and it filtered failures on the one reason
string, so a second settlement under another reason was invisible. The new tests
count failures across every reason:
- `test_outbox_capacity_eviction_is_not_resurrected_by_the_retry_queue` drives
  the retry ladder at a 1ms backoff. It also checks the invariant in count form:
  on an all-failing device, `retry_queue_size() == outbox_entry_count()`.
- `test_outbox_capacity_eviction_is_not_resurrected_by_a_flush` checks that
  `flush_outbox_all` does not re-drive an evicted message.
- `test_outbox_capacity_eviction_while_awaiting_ack_settles_once` covers an
  evicted message whose ACK times out and whose late ACK then arrives.
- `test_media_outbox_capacity_eviction_retires_the_retry_entry` covers the same
  leak in the media outbox, which was silent because the transfer abort is
  idempotent.

**Mutation checks.** Removing the retry-queue line from the helper fails the three
resurrection tests. Removing the ACK-tracker line fails only the awaiting-ACK
test.

**`ensure_outbox_entry` stays** in the retry and flush paths as a guard, and its
comments no longer describe resurrection as intended. I found no other path that
leaves an ACK-requiring message queued for retry without an outbox entry:
- The `initialize_mls` rollback restores the outbox but never enqueues retries.
- Restore never touches the retry queue.

**Not addressed here:**
- Messages that do not require an ACK and whose send fails are enqueued for retry
  without an outbox entry. Because `added_at` is reset on every re-enqueue, such a
  message has no lifetime at all. I have not checked whether any caller of
  `handle_send_failure` sends one.
- A telemetry-side backstop, a rate limit on forwarding `message_failed` with the
  rollup count kept exact, will follow as a separate PR.

prs.title: test(leaf): run the phone interop suite at the wall clock, read once
prs.body:
## Summary

Since 2026-09-18 at 12:12Z, the Test job fails on every branch, main included.
48 of the 65 tests in `offline-protocol-leaf/tests/phone_interop.rs` fail with
the phone refusing the device's key package:

```
the phone accepts the device's key package: InvalidKeyPackage("The lifetime of the leaf node is not valid.")
```

**Why it expired.** The suite ran at a fixed instant,
`NOW = 1_787_314_332` (2026-08-21T12:12:12Z). The fixed date was chosen so the
suite could not expire: control-frame stamps are signed, and the device refuses
a stale one. That reasoning holds for the device, which is told the time. It
does not hold for the phone. The phone is a production `MlsManager`, and its
MLS library checks a key package's lifetime against the system clock, with no
seam to pin it. A device key package minted at `NOW` therefore stopped being
acceptable `LEAF_KEY_PACKAGE_LIFETIME` (28 days) later. Main's last green run
was about six hours before that.

**The fix.** The instant is now the wall clock, read once per test process
through a `OnceLock`. Every stamp and every `handle()` call in a run still sees
the same value, which is the property the fixed date was protecting, and the
phone's own reading agrees with it. Most of the diff is rustfmt re-wrapping
lines that grew when `NOW` became `now()`.

This is test-only. No library code changes.

## Related issues

Unblocks #444 and #445, whose Test jobs fail on this and nothing else.

## Type of change

- [x] `test` — adding or correcting tests

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes (no library change)
- [x] `cargo test -p offline-protocol-leaf` passes: 65 of 65 interop tests, up from 17
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` passes, so no second expired fixture was hiding behind this one (CI stops at the first failing binary)
- [x] `cargo-deny` is satisfied (no dependency changes)
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits
- [x] No new `unsafe`
- [x] The UniFFI UDL did not change

## Breaking changes

None.

## Notes for reviewers

- `tools/embedded-footprint/src/bin/leaf.rs` pins the same instant as
  `PAIRED_AT`. It never reaches a phone-side lifetime check, so it cannot
  expire this way.
- The leaf crate's doc example also pins it, and it only builds a key-package
  frame.
- Neither of those is changed.
